newsitem.title: UK: French company to collect Chinese genes.
newsitem.headline: French company to collect Chinese genes.

text.p: A French genetics company has won a deal that will let it examine the DNA of the entire population of China if it wants, New Scientist magazine reported on Thursday.
Paris-based Genset, which specialises in collecting and sequencing human DNA, says it will appoint about 20 researchers to collect and analyse the information.

But the magazine said geneticists were worried that China could use information gathered by the company to enforce its 1995 Maternal and Infantile Health Care Law, denounced by opponents as a "eugenics" law to stop "inferior" births.
According to New Scientist, Genset is working with a Chinese partner company, Tang Frere International. Its information will be used to develop new diagnostic tests and drugs.
Genet's president, Pascal Brandys, was quoted as saying he did not think the programme would be used across all of China's 1.2 billion population.
"I don't think it will be possible in the short term to do large-scale population screening, although it may become an issue in China in the next millenium," he said.
"We will work towards (new medicines), which will be very different from population screening."

"The Chinese have as much right as anyone else to reap the medical rewards of molecular genetics. And there can be no doubt that the search for new therapies, not eugenics, is what motivates the French scientists," it said in a commentary.

"But...the Chinese government might still attempt to use the knowledge to identify genetically "unfit' couples and foetuses. It might not do so for years, or even decades, but that relieves nobody of their moral responsibilities to act now to make the regime repeal its law."

China's population is considered fertile ground for genetics research because many villages are so isolated. Some villagers are as closely related as families, and many carry traits not seen elsewhere in the world.
